what_this_is: The PRE-REGISTERED red set for rc452's experiment arm (rc452-s2): the Python chain-run reader rebuilds the 'q' wire kind as srmech.math.q.Q, and the nine derived-predicate Class-N ops RETURN Q, with NO acceptance-widening, NO call-site repairs and NO ToolEntry edits. The rc452 ruling enumerated this set IN ADVANCE. It is committed BEFORE the product change so the prediction cannot be fitted to the outcome; every run of _rc452_red_experiment.py embeds this file's git blob hash.
falsification_clause: If the observed red set differs from this manifest in EITHER direction - a red outside it, a predicted red that stays green, or a wrong count at a predicted site - the ruling's projection of the never-executed A-FULL composite is FALSIFIED, judge 3's surviving A-CARRIER placement dissent RE-OPENS, and the build agent must halt and report loudly rather than absorb the surprise. A-CARRIER's own record is 691 passed / 1 honest red, executed end to end; A-FULL was never executed as a whole by any workshop.
enumeration_predicate: A test module is enumerated iff its AST contains a Name, Attribute or string Constant node naming one of the nine Class-N ops (rational_add, rational_mul, rational_div, rational_pow_uint, exp_series_truncate, sin_series_truncate, cos_series_truncate, log1p_series_truncate, atan_series_truncate) - UNION the two chain-wire gates (test_c_cascade_value_parity_rc450.py, test_cascade_catalog_executable_rc420.py). Re-derivable with `_rc452_red_experiment.py --census`.
divergence_from_the_plan: The rc452 plan calls this 'the enumerated 24-file set'. No 24-file list exists anywhere in the ruling or the four workshop reports, so the number could not be reproduced; the stated predicate yields 41 files. 41 is the STRICTLY WIDER set, so it can only make the prediction harder to satisfy, never easier - which is the honest direction for a falsification test. Reported rather than silently reconciled.

native_baseline.requirement: HAS_NATIVE=True, NATIVE_ABI_VERSION=20, EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION=20, LOAD_ERROR=None from a libsrmech.so freshly rebuilt from HEAD
native_baseline.why: A .so built at one ABI against a higher EXPECTED_ABI_VERSION sets HAS_NATIVE=False with every symbol present, so nm -D says yes and every native gate SKIPS silently. A red set measured under that condition would be missing every native-gated site.

baseline_xfails_measured: ONE xfail exists on the enumerated set at the rc451 baseline (measured, not assumed: the first --expect-green run reported it and the run was REJECTED until it was recorded here). It is frozen so that any NEW xfail during the build counts as a RED - marking a failure expected must not buy a green.

predicted_reds.why: raw[0] / raw[1] subscript of cos_series_truncate's now-Q return; Q defines __iter__ but no __getitem__, so this raises TypeError: 'Q' object is not subscriptable. Mechanical fix in rc452-s3: .numerator / .denominator.

neg_sin = (-sin_t[0], sin_t[1]) subscripts sin_series_truncate's now-Q return. Note the two lines below it (s.blocks[1].imag[0] == cos_t) do NOT red: Q.__eq__ coerces a 2-int pair through _as_pair, so tuple == Q is True by the reflected op.
assert nat[1] > 0 on exp_series_truncate's now-Q return; 4 parametrizations (_EXP_ASSERT_ABORT_PINS has 4 entries).
assert nat[1] > 0 inside the 120-draw loop; 5 parametrizations (_SERIES has 5 entries: exp/sin/cos/log1p/atan). The `nat == pure` assert on the line above does NOT red - Q == Q compares exactly.
rational_pow_uint((0, 1), r)[0] subscripts the now-Q return; 5 parametrizations (r in [0,1,2,3,7]).
_reduce_rational(2 * two_cos[0], two_cos[1]) subscripts cos_series_truncate's now-Q return.

assert isinstance(out, tuple) - the shipped pin on the OLD return contract. It is not a defect; it is the contract being changed, and it becomes isinstance(out, Q) in rc452-s3. The one predicted red that is a deliberate contract flip rather than a mechanical accessor edit.

The rational family is NOT CLOSED under its own return type: rational_add/_mul/_div/_pow_uint reject a Q operand (isinstance(a, (tuple, list)) guard at rational.py:739 and peers), so an op cannot consume its own output. Config A found this by attacking its own config; the acceptance-widening in rc452-s3 fixes it with ZERO edits to this test file - which is the executable proof that it was a source defect and not a stale contract.
Same closure defect, same zero-edit requirement.

The shipped GREEN witness at :599-602 REQUIRES the collapse rc452 removes: it asserts the q wire {"d":"6","k":"q","n":"5"} classifies IDENTICAL against the Python 2-tuple (5, 6). Once the reader rebuilds Q, _bits(Q) != _bits((5,6)) and the witness goes DIVERGENT. THIS RED IS THE DELIVERABLE - it flips to required-DIVERGENT in rc452-s5, with a q-vs-Q(5,6) required-IDENTICAL witness shipped beside it. ONLY this one parametrization reds; the other five green witnesses are untouched.

notes_on_what_would_falsify_each_class.subscript sites: If a predicted subscript site stays GREEN, either the op did not in fact change return type on that path (a dispatch arm still returning a tuple - i.e. the return-widening is incomplete) or the site is dead. Both are findings.
notes_on_what_would_falsify_each_class.closure defects: If the two cosmos reds do NOT appear, the rational family was already closed under Q and Config A's finding (3) is wrong - which would shrink the ruled change by one arm and is reportable either way.
notes_on_what_would_falsify_each_class.the witness: If the parity witness stays GREEN, the reader change did not reach the comparator, and the entire discrimination claim (Config C's 39/39 two-arm experiment) is unreproduced on this tree.
